pairs.difference: A: the cone has soft satin grey metal with small rivets and thin panel seams, and the porthole alone carries a sharp highlight, so matte and shiny mix as on the real cards. B: the envelope has a soft embossed paper edge, but the postcard is packed with crisp windows, shutters and bushes, and the postmark rings are raised like piping. detail_subject (0.0499) and gloss_share (0.186) sit above the real range.
pairs.fix: Keep the postcard picture simple, with a few soft color shapes and no tiny windows. Print the postmark flat into matte paper in thin ink lines, not raised. Keep the paper dull with no sheen.

pairs.difference: A: the inflatable has glossy vinyl with fine puckered seams along the tubes, which matches the puckers on the real neck pillow. B: the asteroid has matte grey rock with a fine grain and soft craters, and glossier pink crystals. Both materials read true, and all measures are in range.

A: the tower walls carry stray scratched brick-line marks that follow no pattern, and the sand surface looks smooth and waxy rather than grainy, with sand grain only on the beach. B: the stone blocks have clean soft seams, the dome is satin, and the telescope brass is shinier, a quiet mix like the real lighthouse.
pairs.fix: Make the castle walls packed damp sand with a very fine, even grain. Remove the scratched brick lines. Press in only soft, shallow marks from the mold.

pairs.difference: A: the ice is marbled with thin veins and the tail is wispy, smeared white streaks, with highlight_share at 0.219 above the real range. The mark-making looks like AI smear rather than a surface. B: the scarf is soft matte cloth with folds, set against a shinier gold badge. It has no weave, but it is smooth and quiet like the real curtain and pillow.
pairs.fix: Paint the ice as clean flat facets with a few sharp highlights and no thin veins. Make the tail a smooth soft gradient without streaks, and keep the white glow small.

pairs.difference: A: the ball is blurred and smeared. The white highlight is blown out into a fuzzy blob, the panel joins have no welded seam, and pink bleeds along the color edges. detail_subject (0.0103), micro_texture (0.0044) and gloss_share (0.005) fall below the real range. B: the glass, ice and lime are crisp with small droplets and sit at the top of the range. It is busy, but the materials are distinct.
pairs.fix: Draw the ball as thin shiny vinyl with a crisp, small window highlight. Add thin welded seams between the panels and a slightly raised valve cap. Keep the color edges clean.

pairs.difference: A: the station has satin white hull panels with thin seams and a clean glowing stripe, at the upper edge of the real range. B: red paint, the grey rack and the wheels all carry the same streaky, wet, brushy gloss, and the small parts, spokes and bolts are dense and smeared. detail_subject (0.1042), micro_texture (0.036) and gloss_share (0.308) all exceed real cards.
pairs.fix: Use fewer, cleaner parts. Make the bike frame smooth painted metal with one thin highlight, the tires matte rubber and the car body satin. Remove streaky brush marks.

pairs.difference: A: the bag has an even canvas weave across the whole body and a neatly dashed stitched patch, the same added fine dashed stitching seen on the generated gloves in the lessons. B: the target is smooth and the teddy reads as smooth plastic rather than fur, but its surfaces are soft and quiet. The call is weak because A's fabric does read as fabric.
pairs.fix: Quiet the weave so the cloth reads as soft smooth canvas, with only a faint texture. Replace the thin dashed stitches with a few soft pressed seams.

pairs.difference: A: the plant and pot are one soft satin clay finish, with a gentle highlight, and detail stays quiet. B: the table has large streaky wood stripes, the stickers have hard crisp white edges, and the cover is sharply detailed. The grain is big and decorative, and detail_subject (0.0493) sits at the top of the range.
pairs.fix: Make the wood grain fine and faint, with thin lines at low contrast. Soften the sticker edges. Give the book cover a matte, slightly worn cloth finish.

pairs.difference: A: the rocket has soft satin metal with small rivets, panel seams and a shiny porthole, close to the real submarine. B: the bar counter has speckled noise over the concrete, the thatch is big chunky slats, and the pineapple and stools are heavily lacquered. Texture scale is too big and the grain reads as visible noise.
pairs.fix: Make the counter smooth plaster with very faint fine speckle. Draw the thatch as thin fine strands rather than wide slats. Keep the stool tops matte.

pairs.difference: A: the globe has deep blue lacquer with a soft highlight, and raised gold stars and a brass stand with sharp reflections, a good gloss mix. B: the balloons are airbrushed and blurry, with fuzzy pale highlights and no crisp reflection, so the latex reads as soft matte foam. detail_subject (0.0072), micro_texture (0.0022) and gloss_share (0.0) fall below the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the balloons shiny stretched latex, with a small crisp window highlight on each, a thin rim light, and darker tied necks with fine wrinkles.

pairs.difference: A: the parchment is a flat pale cream with no fibers or edge wear, the blue lines have soft halos, and highlight_share (0.254) exceeds the real range while gloss_share (0.027) falls below it, so it reads washed out. B: the paper is matte, with a soft satin ribbon, a gold seal and a glossy table, showing clear separation of finishes.
pairs.fix: Give the parchment a faint fine paper grain with slight darker aging at the edges. Draw the ink lines thin and clean with no glow. Keep the paper from washing out to white.

pairs.difference: A: the cans and bottles behind the glass melt into blurred smears, the labels dissolve, and the condensation dots read as noise over the crop. B: the tube has crinkled foil metal and a fine ribbed cap, a very clear material, though it is more photographic than the real cards. The smear in A is the stronger flaw.
pairs.fix: Draw the cans and bottles clean and sharp behind clear glass, with simple labels. Use only a few larger water drops. Make the machine body satin painted metal, not glowing plastic.

pattern: Generated cards still miss the even, quiet finish of the real ones in one of three ways. Some add fine detail everywhere, such as dense crisp small parts and dashed stitches. Some use texture at the wrong scale, such as chunky thatch, streaky wood, or speckled noise and stray scratch marks. Some go the other way and are blurry and airbrushed, with fuzzy highlights, smeared labels and color bleed, so shiny materials lose their crisp reflection. Across those cases, gloss is either the same wet sheen on every part or nearly absent, rather than the matte and shiny mix that real cards hold within one object.
